# Review — cid-tiradas-19-23 (lines 404–492)

## Pass 1 — units.json

**Continuity (after edits):** PASS. 39 units; concatenated `t` = the packet's 99 lines exactly, in print order
(398 after 415; 441b–441e, 443b, 446b, 464b, 477b, 481b included); every `l` has as many lines as its `t`; all
units 1–5 lines; `p: true` on the first unit of each of the five tiradas. `t` untouched (checked by script against
the draft as received).

**441b–441e (point a).** These numbers are ours, not Pidal's. On PDF p. 159 (printed p. 155) the margin has 440 at
"Vos con çiento", nothing at "pues que a Castejón" (441 by count), nothing at the four italic lines (en él
fincaredes … / a mí dedes … / con Dios e vuestra auze … / Dixo el Campeador …), nothing at "vos con los dozientos"
(442) and "allá vaya" (443), then a printed 443b at "e Galín Garciaz". Pidal prints the restored lines wholly in
italics and without numbers. The establish log says only "confirmed and marked"; conventions.md already gives the
rule (unnumbered italic lines take provisional letters after the preceding number). The u16 note now says so,
in the words of the published 181b–d note (cid-tiradas-10-14). The four lines are split across u16 (441b–d)
and u17 (441e); u17's note says that 441e is the last restored line. `auze` is confirmed on the image (italic z).

**Pidal's footnotes on these pages** (PDF pp. 156–161) were read and used as the lexical aid the conventions
allow: 405, 409, 415/398 (Atienza), 417, 421, 427, 429, 435, 442, 446, 451, 459, 473 (ela), 475 (preçia'),
477 (prear), 481 (gañado), 481b, 483, 485, 486, 489, 492. Several draft notes said things that went against
them; those are fixed below.

**Assonance** worked out again from all 99 line-endings: 19 ó (noch … santigó); 20 á (acomend[ar], a, cavalgar,
más, posar, han); 21 ó with ó-e (sol, Campeador, son, pendones); 22 á with á-e/á-i (salue, cavalgue, Fenares, trae,
nadi); 23 á-a throughout (ganançia, heredanças, fincar[a]n, andan, preavan … counting). The claims are right,
except that u7 cited the wrong tirada.

**Cross-references** (36 cited lines): each one was checked against the published parts (pilot by unit, the
others by their packets) and against this packet. They all point to the right line, except "as in tirada 18" (u7)
and "two lines on" (u1).

**Point (b) crieban.** The form is the present tense, not the imperfect. In crebar (the old form of quebrar) the
stressed e becomes ie: criebo, crieba, crieban. Add the present ending -an and you get crieban = quiebran. An
imperfect of a first-conjugation verb would be crebavan. The -ié- imperfect of -er/-ir verbs is -ién (querién)
and has no b. The drafter's sense, 'they break', is right. The gloss ('imperfect, = quebraban') was wrong. Units
and gloss now agree: present, = quiebran. The units note also dropped "He reads it as", which gave Pidal a
reading he does not state, and "the form is not certain": once the letters are restored, the form is plain. The
restoration itself is marked as Pidal's.

**Point (c).** 414 "es dia a de plazo": a = impersonal aver. The note keeps it marked as uncertain, and the day
count against vv. 306–402 checks (three days left at 307; nights at Cardeña, Spinaz de Can and La Figueruela).
The conclusion is now worded as following from that reading, not stated as fact. 475 preçia': Pidal's note
gives preçian, with its n merged into the n of nada. The verb is therefore plural, which rules out the draft's
alternative "or the Çid's"; the force of the line is still marked uncertain. 490 enbiás: kept as "most likely"
an apocopated imperfect subjunctive and marked uncertain. 462 fincar[a]n: the "often a pluperfect" claim is
hedged; the italic a was checked on the image. 441d auze: the etymology was stated as fact and is now "usually
traced to"; the sense is marked uncertain. 473 ela: the draft said ela was "written as one word with y", which
is false (y ela). Pidal's note calls it the archaic feminine article, which he admits from a correction in the
manuscript made in Per Abbat's own time.

### Considered and refused
- Point (b)'s premise that -ieban is an imperfect ending. Refused: see above. The ie is the diphthong of the stem and -an is the present ending.
- u5 analysis of 414 (a = impersonal 'there is'). Kept. It is marked as the likeliest reading of a hard line.
- u38 enbiás and u26 fincar[a]n. Kept as analysed, marked uncertain or hedged (above).
- u14, u20 hedges ("most likely Castejón de Henares", "likely, not certain") where Pidal's notes 435, 446 identify the places outright. Kept: harmless, and the published parts hedge places the same way.
- u8 "whoever wishes to eat (let him eat)" against Pidal's paraphrase 'bien'. Kept: both supply the verb the line leaves out, and they come to the same sense.
- u15 "Álvar Fáñez Minaya" in `i`, in the text's order, not the house "Minaya Álvar Fáñez". Kept: the house rendering is for the text's Minaya Albar Fáñez; here the text puts Minaya last.
- u26 i "scattered over the fields": slightly expanded. Kept: v. 460 says they went out to their fields.
- u28 n "captives were sold or held for ransom" and u22 n "España … the whole peninsula". Kept: general and accurate.
- u16 personal a in "since that Castejón we-shall-draw-out": already without "to". No change.
- No English in `i` read like a remembered translation. Every `i` was checked against its `l`. The changes above are fidelity changes.

## Pass 2 — gloss.json

Keys = the 175 novel-forms.json keys exactly, plus `__broaden__`. Every token of the 99 lines (brackets stripped,
lowercased, apostrophe split) is covered by gloss.json or known-forms.json. There are no missing and no extra
keys, and known-forms.json matches cid-glossary.json. Every entry was checked against its line(s) and the units'
notes after Pass 1. Each of the 23 draft broadens began with the old entry whole + " · ". Six broadens were added
for known forms used in a new sense, and all 29 were re-checked by script. The units' continuity check was run
again after Pass 2: PASS (99/99).

## For the owner
- **v. 397 in the published cid-tiradas-18-18 goes against Pidal's note.** It renders de siniestro Sant Estevan as "on his left San Esteban". Pidal's note on 397 (PDF p. 155) says the opposite: the Çid passes on the left of San Esteban, and San Esteban is not on the traveller's left. His note on 415 reads de diestro Atiença at v. 398 the same way. This part now follows Pidal at 398. There are two ways to make the parts agree: correct 18-18 u(396–399) to Pidal, or put 398 back to the plain reading. The owner should choose.
- **Personal a in `l`** is handled unevenly across the published parts ("to thee I-adore", "to the his daughters", "thou-raisedst Lazarus"). Here it is now dropped throughout, following the 18-18 review. A house rule would settle it.
